verdict.rationale: Tavily's core API/SDK accepts natural-language strings directly as inputs (search, crawl instructions, research topics), and the official MCP server lets any MCP-compatible AI client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.) invoke Tavily's search/extract tools purely via natural-language agent commands. This directly satisfies an AI-native user's need to operate the product conversationally rather than through rigid syntax. missing for 10: independent/hands-on reports confirming natural-language MCP commands work reliably in practice, and a broader conversational command surface beyond search/crawl/research query strings
